- 2026-10-04: Reading a `windows-mutants` dispatch while it runs: `gh run view --job <id> --log` refuses until EVERY job of the run has finished, so a finished job's log reads through `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/actions/jobs/<id>/logs --allow-escape-sequences` (without the flag it refuses the ANSI output), with the escapes stripped before grepping. Each job's harness document is its `{"v":1,"cmd":"run",…}` line, and the outcome lines carry every mutant's grade: read a MISSED line's cfg from source before calling it a survivor.

- 2026-10-04: A dispatched run joins its sha's checks: `ci.py conclusion --sha <sha>` after a `windows-mutants` dispatch reads the dispatch's six `mutants (…)` checks too (15 → 21 on the measured commit), so the push's CI verdict is read before the dispatch, and the dispatch's own verdict row with `--name mutants`. [corrected 2026-10-10: nine `mutants (…)` checks since the root package was split by file, 15 → 24 as read on the dispatch of that day] [corrected 2026-10-13: ten `mutants (…)` checks since `viola-cmd-verify-stop` joined the matrix; no dispatch has read the new total]

- 2026-10-09: `gh run list --commit` takes the full 40-character sha: given an abbreviated one it prints an empty list with exit 0 while a run exists on that commit, which reads as "no run". Pass `$(git rev-parse HEAD)`, and never read an empty list from a short sha as an absence.

Path-scoped rules for viola's event log and state: the normalised event kinds, the `events.ndjson` line, snapshots and the hook → kind mapping. Authoritative source: `.andromeda/architecture.md` §Standard Contracts + §Conventions (Naming patterns, Data model conventions). There is no broker: the log on disk is the single source of truth.

- `{"v":1,"ts":"<RFC3339 ms Z>","instance":"<ViolaName>","kind":"<kind>","source":"hook|wrapper|cli","data":{}}` — one complete object + `\n` per single `write` call; multi-line text travels as an escaped string.
- `data` is kind-specific and uses only viola's normalised fields; it never embeds a raw Claude payload.

- Normalised kinds live only in `viola-core`, never with Claude-specific names: `session-start`, `turn-ended`, `prompt-submitted`, `question`, `permission`, `plan`, `session-end`, `activity`, `link`, `unlink`, `wheel`, `budget-gate`, `send-issued` `{cursor, from?}`, `send-confirmed` `{cursor, confirmed?}` (`confirmed:false` only for an unconfirmable send), `send-refused` `{refusal, detail, cursor?}` (the CL-1 send records, `source: wrapper`; `cursor` absent for a refusal before `send-issued`), `dialog-expired` `{dialog_id, dialog_kind}` (`source: wrapper`, appended once when a held dialog's hold ends; it carries no question, plan or tool text).

- `wait` wakes only on `turn-ended`, `question`, `permission`, `plan`, `session-end`, `dialog-expired` (the one wrapper-appended kind that wakes it, appended through `WaitFeed::appending`); `activity`, `link`, `unlink`, `wheel`, `budget-gate` and the send records are log-only.

- SessionStart → `session-start` (`cause` startup|clear|resume|compact|unknown, `agent_session_id`); UserPromptSubmit → `prompt-submitted` (`text` normalised: long-paste wrapper removed, then tag escaping reversed; `origin` driver|human|harness — the hook files only human|harness, and `driver` comes only from the wrapper's relabel of the in-flight send's own prompt, matched exactly on the send's typed text, the sent text with every CR LF pair and every other CR as one LF and without its trailing CR and LF characters); PreToolUse AskUserQuestion → `question`; PreToolUse ExitPlanMode → `plan`; PermissionRequest → `permission` (a PermissionRequest repeating the armed `question` / `plan` dialog's tool with an equal `tool_input` is that dialog's continuation and raises no event); Stop → `turn-ended` (`last_assistant_message` or `null`; `background_tasks`, the Stop payload's `background_tasks` array length, a count only, or `null` when the key is absent, `null` or not an array); SessionEnd → `session-end`; Notification / PostToolUse / PostToolUseFailure → `activity`.

- Dialog hooks send only `hook.dialog`; the wrapper assigns `dialog_id` (monotonic, restored from the log on start) and appends the dialog event before it can wake `wait` or reply — even when it replies `null`. At most one dialog pending per instance.

- Harness turns (a prompt whose raw start is `<agent-message from=`, `<task-notification>`, `<\cross-session-message` or `<cross-session-message`) are `origin:"harness"` and never flip the wheel. The escaped cross-session form is the one escaped tag that classifies, so a human typing it at a prompt's start is filed `harness` (founder-ratified, 2026-09-29). As measured on 2.1.287, a human who types `<task-notification>` at a prompt's start is filed `harness` too.
- `wait after` and the `send` `cursor` are byte offsets into the instance's `events.ndjson`: never truncate, rotate or rewrite it; instance dirs are reused and appended to.

- The link set is derived by replaying `link`/`unlink`; a repeated pair adds no line. The driven wrapper appends `link` (`source: wrapper`, `{driver, driven}`) once per new pair, for an issued `send` (directly before its `send-issued`), a taken `answer` whose `from` is another instance's name, or a served `link` call; a refused call, a call with no `from` and one under the wrapper's own name link nothing. `since` is that line's `ts`, and the wrapper restores the set from the log at every start (`src/run/links.rs`). The wrapper serves `link` `{driver, driven}` → `{since, already_linked}` and `unlink` `{driver, driven}` → `{}` (the verbs `viola link` / `viola unlink <driver> <driven> [--json]`; neither method reads `from`): a `link` of a held pair appends nothing and answers its `since` with `already_linked: true`; `unlink` appends `unlink` (`source: wrapper`, `{driver, driven}`) once per held pair it removes (`LinkSet::remove`) and answers `{}` either way; a missing, non-string or invalid name, a `driven` that is not the wrapper's own name and a `driver` equal to `driven` are each `-32602` with no line; each answers only after its event line and the snapshot write.

- Envelope `{"v":1,"written_at","writer","data"}`, replaced atomically (tempfile `persist` through the one shared helper `viola_state::fs::replace_private`); only the instance's wrapper writes `instances/<name>/snapshot.json`, and it rewrites the snapshot's `agent_session_id` on each `session-start`, so the `claude agents --json` session-id join survives a `/clear`; it writes `pending_dialog` `{dialog_id, kind}` before the dialog's event line is appended and back to none when that append fails, so a reader that sees the line already sees it.

- An unsupported `v` or a parse failure → ignore the snapshot and replay the log; replay recovers only `links`, `agent_session_id`, `wheel`, `budget_paused`, `budget_override_until` (`dialog_pending` reads false). The wrapper's budget gate writes `budget-gate` `{paused, window?, override_until?}` once at start as record two and then only when the triple (paused, window, override end) changes, and mirrors it to the snapshot's `budget_paused` / `budget_override_until` in the same step. As landed the classified read and the replay are library code (`viola_state::snapshot::read_snapshot_classified`, `viola_state::replay`) with six product readers, each after the instance's strict-modes check has passed: `viola revive`'s preflight (one read for both its collision check and its recorded directory), `viola list`'s `viola_state::board::read` (a replayed snapshot gives a `live` row only for a beat at most `STALE_AFTER` old, never `stale`), `viola_state::liveness::live_endpoint` (the CLI frame verbs, `viola link` / `viola unlink` and `viola mcp`'s frame tools; only a real snapshot gives an endpoint), `viola hook`'s `connect` (a replayed or absent snapshot is unreachable, so the hook fails open), `hook statusline`'s `serve` (a replayed snapshot holds no `statusline_command`, so nothing runs) and `run`'s collision check (a replayed snapshot judged by the heartbeat alone: `already-live` within `STALE_AFTER`, else free); no product code under `src/` calls `read_snapshot`. The replay writes no file, gives no `cwd` (a revive over a replayed snapshot is refused `cwd-missing`), and recovers `links` from the logged `link` / `unlink` lines in its one pass through `replay::apply_link_line` (a `link` line with no string `ts` reads `since: "unknown"`). `replay::session_chain` reads the logged session ids in one pass and logs nothing.

- Heartbeat touched every 1 s. A snapshot pid that is dead, or alive with another start time, is `gone` whatever the beat; otherwise a beat ≤ 5 s old is `live`, an older or absent one `stale`. Never a bare pid. The snapshot's `pid` and `started_at` are also the server identity: `viola_state::liveness::live_endpoint` returns them with the endpoint from one `replay::read_snapshot_or_replay` (`LiveEndpoint`, only on a real snapshot: a replayed or absent one, a failed read or a stale wrapper gives none; where it gives none, `viola_state::liveness::without_endpoint`, behind the strict-modes check at every caller, reads the cause through `symlink_metadata`, opening nothing and writing no line: a directory reads `InstanceDead`, so a frame verb against a stale instance reads `instance-dead`, and anything else `UnwrappedName`), and every frame-writing client (CLI `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` / `pause` / `release` / `link` / `unlink`, `hook.event` / `hook.dialog`, the MCP `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` tools) runs the instance's strict-modes check first (`client::refuse_untrusted` for the CLI verbs, the hook's `trusted` for `hook.event` / `hook.dialog`, `strict::check_instance` in the MCP frame tools; a refused check writes no frame and no line), then takes its snapshot read (the CLI frame verbs and the MCP tools the liveness-only pre-check through `live_endpoint`, `viola hook`'s event and dialog paths one shared `replay::read_snapshot_or_replay`, a replayed or absent snapshot read as unreachable), then checks the recorded endpoint's directory (`viola_state::strict::check_endpoint_dir`; a refusal reads `socket-dir-refused` and writes one `process-exit` at the CLI, one `hook-decision` at the hook and no line at MCP), then connects (the hook through `Client::connect_by`), then, on Unix, refuses a connected peer of another euid or one it cannot read (`viola_channel::peer_admitted` over `server_euid`; a refusal reads `server-verify-failed`), then, on Linux and Windows, compares the connected peer's pid and its OS start time with them before its first frame (`verify_server` → the closed `ServerVerdict` `Matches` · `Mismatch` · `Unverifiable`); a refused directory, a refused euid, a mismatch, or a check that cannot be made, writes no frame. macOS reports no peer pid, so `server_verdict` returns `Matches` with no comparison: the recorded gap, owned by no route entry; the socket-directory and euid checks stand built there, so on macOS `server-verify-failed` means an euid mismatch alone.

- The next append heals a torn last line: under the log's lock it writes one LF ahead of its line in the same single write, and logs one `state-recovered` line. A reader never writes. The one reader `events::read_from` counts what it steps over, per read, as `skipped{unknown_kinds, unknown_fields, torn_lines}`, never fatal: an unterminated last line, an over-long line and a line that is not one object are torn; a line of an unknown kind is not returned; a known-kind line with a key outside its contract is returned and counted once. `viola list` is the first surface that shows them: `list --json`'s `skipped` `{unknown_kinds, unknown_fields, torn_lines}` and the BAY line's `skipped a - b - c`, each summed over every scanned instance, gone ones included. External payloads parse tolerantly (`#[serde(default)]`, `Option<T>`, no `deny_unknown_fields`), with serde_path_to_error drift reports going to the instance detail file only.
- Lock files are separate siblings (`<name>.lock`): append + exclusive lock fails on Windows.
- Timestamps via chrono `to_rfc3339_opts(SecondsFormat::Millis, true)`; malformed external values become `"unknown"`, never an error. JSON fields snake_case, enum values kebab-case.

Path-scoped rules for viola's one built design surface, human CLI output (cli); the web-spa frontend is deferred to 0.2.0, its technology is not chosen, and 0.1.0 renders no page. Authoritative sources: `.andromeda/design-system.md` and `.andromeda/layout-templates.md`.

title: Tokens (the Token Test; a 0.2.0 frontend design input, 0.1.0 renders no page)

data.head: ## Tokens (the Token Test; a 0.2.0 frontend design input, 0.1.0 renders no page)

body: - Exactly eight hex values (`--c-*`), read only where a role alias is assigned; components use role aliases (`--surface-*`, `--ink*`, `--rule-*`, `--attention`, `--handoff`, `--focus-ring`, `--rb-*`). Every length is a token or a `ch` track in `--strip-cols` / `--strip-cols-wrapped` / `--tape-cols`; only the `760px` / `1024px` breakpoints are literal.
- Amber means `dialog_pending` only; blue means handoff only. Lamp-off, amber and blue text never sit on holder `#2A2E33` (they fail AA there).
- Borders-only depth: no `box-shadow`, `text-shadow`, glow or `drop-shadow`; radius 0 everywhere; dark only.

- Fonts: installed stacks only (`--font-label` Bahnschrift…, `--font-field` Cascadia Mono…); every contrast and render assertion must hold with the Linux DejaVu families resolved (the resolved family, not only the declared stack); 0.1.0 renders no page, so no CI step renders these stacks.

title: Motion (base expression 0.2; the frontend's level deferred to 0.2.0)

data.head: ## Motion (base expression 0.2; the frontend's level deferred to 0.2.0)

body: - At the base expression 0.2 the duration scale's 0.0–0.2 row applies (0–100ms, no entrance), and the cli (0.2 on a TTY, 0.0 otherwise) has no motion at all; the cocked strip's 12px / 160ms translate is a 0.2.0 frontend design input.

- The web components are 0.2.0 frontend design; 0.1.0 renders no page. The six captions NAME · LIVE · STATUS · WHEEL · DIALOG · CLI, their words and slot order are fixed, and a future page reuses them; the readback vocabulary is `open`, `read back`, `unable`, `unconfirmable`.
- Nothing is shown as delivered until read back; `turn-ended` never fills a box.

- Colour decision order (first match → no colour): `--json` · `viola run` · `viola hook`/`mcp` · `NO_COLOR` (present, an empty value included) · `TERM=dumb` · non-TTY stdout · Windows VT enable failed. SGR only for amber `DIALOG`, dim `stale` rows, bold NAME — always beside its word; never on `unable` / `fail`. As built (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline), `list` is uncoloured under any rung above; on a terminal that takes colour every NAME value is bold, the `DIALOG` word of a wrapped row with a pending dialog takes the attention token (its kind word plain), a wrapped `stale` row is dim from its first byte to its last (NAME dim and bold; on a stale row with a dialog only `DIALOG` amber and not dim), the BAY line, caption, empty-board line and separator carry no SGR, the spans are laid over the escaped, padded cells (the plain board's columns, one write), and the depth is truecolor / 256 / 16 from `COLORTERM` / `TERM` (256 on Windows once VT enabling has succeeded) (`COLUMNS`, `CLICOLOR`, `CLICOLOR_FORCE` and `CI` are not read). A wrapped row joined to one `claude agents --json` read by child pid or agent session id reads STATUS `idle` or `busy`, else `unknown`; each unjoined session follows under the `-- UNWRAPPED - READ-ONLY --` line, sorted by name, NAME its `sessionId`, LIVE `live`, `n/a` in WHEEL, DIALOG and CLI, with no separator when there is none and the board as with no `claude` on a failed read. With the terminal's width known (`viola_pty::host_size()`, never `COLUMNS`) only an unwrapped NAME is cut, to the column less 3 characters plus `...`, never inside an escape; a wrapped NAME is never cut, and a piped board or `--json` keeps every name whole.

- stdout = results (`viola mcp` writes only MCP frames, and exits 1 with nothing on stdout or stderr when its home or `diagnostics/` fails `check_path`); stderr = the TTY-only context lines (`waiting:`, the send issue line, `last`'s header), `last`'s `no message` for `null`, refusals `unable  <name>  <reason>  <detail>` (the exit-1 refusals of `run` / `revive` / `verify`, a `verify` stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM before its rows are checked (stdout empty, no summary), `list`'s exit-21 strict-modes refusal, `plugin install`'s exit-21 strict-modes refusal (the home pair, stdout empty; under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document, stderr empty) `link` / `unlink`'s exit-21 strict-modes refusal of the driven instance (`revive`'s instance pair naming it, stdout empty; under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document, stderr empty) and the exit-21 strict-modes refusal `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause` and `release` make of their instance before any frame (the same instance pair naming it, not the `[/ ]` mirror, stdout empty, no line written; under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document, stderr empty) take the fixed form `unable: <text>`) + one `hint:` line (none under `--json`; there exit 21's document `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"<cause>"}` names its cause, one of `strict-modes-failed` · `instance-dead` · `unwrapped-name` · `endpoint-lost` · `server-verify-failed` · `socket-dir-refused`, the strict-modes refusals above reading `strict-modes-failed`; every refusal of the start `viola revive` shares with `run` is one stdout document `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` with stderr empty, a `pump_child` error printing none, the child having held the terminal, and an oversize `viola answer` / an unusable `viola send` exit 2 with their fixed `UNUSABLE_RESPONSE` / `UNUSABLE_TEXT` stderr line and no document), errors (under `--json` the `cli` catch site prints `{"v":1,"error":"internal-error","detail":null}` on stdout in place of `error: internal error`, stderr then empty; `run`, `revive`'s start, `mcp` and `hook` stay silent at that site). ASCII only (`->`, `[RB]` / `[  ]` / `[/ ]`, ` - `); no spinner, no redraw, no stack traces, no "done". `viola --help` (and `viola help`) prints exactly `Usage: viola [--home <dir>] <verb> [args]`, the served-verb rows `board:` · `traffic:` · `wheel:` · `handoff:` · `setup:` (`handoff:` holding `link, unlink`, `setup:` holding `plugin install`), then `Options:` (no about line, no clap `Commands:` list; pinned by the `HELP` literal in `tests/cli_output_plain.rs`); per-verb `--help` is clap's usage, unchanged; the hidden `viola mcp` (`#[command(hide = true)]`, no argument but the global `--home`, run only by the plugin, never by a person) appears in no row, and the `HELP` literal is unchanged.

- `list` rows escape every control character (C0 with `\n`/`\t`, DEL, C1) as two-hex-digit escape text (`escape_row`); `wait`/`last` text, and a `link` line's `since` that is no RFC 3339 instant, escape C0, DEL and C1 the same way but keep `\n`/`\t`; nothing is stripped. No hint ever names `viola release`; no hint for `unknown`, `wrapper fault` or `internal error`.

Shell mechanics of the Bash tool on this host: the recurring ways a recipe breaks. Every rule is measured on live
work, not hypothetical.

- The working directory MAY persist across calls (measured both ways on one host: persisted in one session,
  reset after every call in another) — rely on neither: anchor every cross-call path absolutely, or `cd` only
  inside a subshell `( cd X && … )` (setup's Bash guard denies a `cd` that would move the cwd); a
  `cd` inside a compound command can also trip a permission prompt.

- A zero-is-healthy count probe (`grep -c` / `grep -q`) exits non-zero on no matches and aborts a
  `&&` chain — suffix `|| true`, or chain with `;`.

- Never build JSON — or any multi-KB document — through shell quoting: `printf` collapses escapes
  content-dependently.

- Documents: the Write tool, whole-content (setup's Bash guard refuses a `cat`/`tee` heredoc with a file
  target). Ledger appends: a VALIDATED python append (`json.dumps(json.loads(...))` — a mangled payload fails
  loudly instead of landing).

- Inline `python -c` is fine for a SHORT, quote-free, single-expression probe; anything longer,
  quote-bearing, or document-carrying goes through a scratchpad file run by path (the measured failure
  modes are size and unquoted expansion, not inlining or quoted heredocs).

- `rm -rf` + `mkdir` + launch compounds get denied by permission layers and abort mid-chain —
  granular steps, fresh unique dirs, no `rm` in a launch path.
- `;` over `&&` for optional probes: an optional probe's failure must not abort the chain.

- Never `pgrep -f` / `pkill -f` on a pattern the invoking shell's own command line contains — it matches, and
  kills, that shell. Select by `ps -eo pid,comm,args` and act on the pid.

- Read `$?` from the BARE command — `| tail` / `| head` report the pipe's LAST command's exit
  (measured green-masking red gates). Redirect output to a file and inspect the file.
- When a tool prints its own verdict, the printed text outranks an unisolated `$?`.

- Heredoc terminators must be column-0 and whitespace-exact — a padded terminator silently
  swallows the rest of the script.

- The repo pins LF through `.gitattributes` (setup appends the lines): `git ls-files --eol` on a pipeline file
  reads `i/lf w/lf`. Never write CRLF into a pipeline file, and never fix a terminator reading with a
  terminator-agnostic script.
- 2026-09-24: `grep` over a glob that matches ONE file prints no `file:` prefix, so an exemption keyed on `^[^:]+:[0-9]+:` never matches — use `grep -H` whenever a later stage parses the prefix.

- 2026-09-28: The Bash guard refuses a heredoc whose payload carries a doubled backslash, so a source edit holding escape sequences (a Rust string literal) goes through the Edit tool, never a shell heredoc. Extended 2026-09-29: it refuses ANY command carrying one — a sed expression, an inline regex, a JSON record — so such a payload goes in a Write-tool file run by path, or builds the backslash with `chr(92)`. Extended 2026-09-29: it also refuses a heredoc redirected to a file (`cat <<'EOF' > f`) — write the file with the Write tool.

- 2026-10-07: On the Linux dev host a process named `viola` is not this repository's by its name: the overseer pair's bridge is another tree's build of the same name, so `pgrep -x viola` reads it too — decide whose a process is by `/proc/<pid>/exe` against the repository root. Extended 2026-10-19: `gate.py census --args target/debug/viola` matches that bridge too — key a census on `projects/viola/target/debug/viola`. Extended 2026-10-27: a process whose binary was rebuilt under it reads `/proc/<pid>/exe` as `<path> (deleted)`, so strip that suffix before comparing.

- 2026-10-07: A removal the permission layer denied is never done through another tool (no script, no re-spelled `rm`): move a scratch home this builder made by its full name into `target/e2e-home.disk/`, read back that `target/e2e-home` no longer holds it, and record where it stands; its deletion is the founder's at the desk (the overseer's direction). Extended 2026-10-16: a tracked repository directory is no scratch home — the classifier refuses moving it aside too, so its removal is the founder's at the desk, and the block that needs it gone runs with its absence guard red, re-fired once he has removed it.

- 2026-10-07: A backgrounded command's output file ends with the harness's own exit line, never the command's last line, so a wait that tests the file's last line for a summary runs to its bound: match the summary anywhere in the file, or wait on the completion notice.

- 2026-10-08: On the Linux dev host the desktop lock is the shell's own, so a search for a locker process and logind's `LockedHint` both read "not locked" while it holds, and no window takes keyboard focus under it: read `hyprctl locked` first before any step that focuses a window or types a key with `wtype`, and stop on `true` (unlocking is the founder's).

- 2026-10-10: The shell variable `TMPDIR` is unset on this host, so a redirect written against it lands at the filesystem root and the command never runs: write scratch output under the session scratchpad's path.

- 2026-10-17: An ad hoc `viola list` typed in the session's own shell reads the host's real `claude agents --json`, every live session on the machine: a probe of `list` puts the fake agent first on its `PATH`, as the tests do.
- 2026-10-27: Read a process listing whole before naming what runs or hangs: a `| head -N` cut hides every row past N, so a status built on it misses live processes.

Path-scoped rules for product code that logs, spans or handles errors. Authoritative source: `.andromeda/obs-plan.md` (tier Standard with Minimal exporter carve-outs); the log format itself is bound to `.andromeda/test-plan.md` §3.

- **Library:** tracing 0.1.44 in every instrumentable crate; tracing-subscriber 0.3.23 (`default-features = false`, `fmt,json,registry,std`) as a product dependency in the root bin only (`viola-channel` and `viola-state` take it as a dev-dependency for their unit tests' line capture). No OTel SDK, no exporter, no reporter (sentry banned), no `tracing-appender`, no `metrics` instruments, no `/metrics` route.

- **Builder:** `fmt().json().flatten_event(true).with_current_span(false).with_span_list(false).with_ansi(false).log_internal_errors(false)`, `MillisUtc` timer (RFC 3339 UTC ms + `Z`), explicit writer — never the stdout default.

- **Levels:** `filter::Targets` from `config.json` `diagnostics_level` (`info` | `debug`); never `RUST_LOG` / `EnvFilter` / the `env-filter` feature. Third-party targets (`rmcp`, `portable_pty`, `sysinfo`, `interprocess`) are OFF; capture their failures from returned `Result`s at viola's seam.

- Codes-only role files: `<home>/diagnostics/{run-<name>,hook-<name>,mcp,cli-<name>}.ndjson`; `mcp` always writes `mcp.ndjson` (D-09), stderr JSON only when that file cannot be opened, never stdout (it carries MCP frames). Content-bearing records (anyhow chain, drift report, panic payload + backtrace) only in `<home>/instances/<name>/diagnostics/detail-<process>.ndjson`, written by the root-bin detail writer, never through the subscriber.

- 0600 files in 0700 dirs; `OpenOptions::append`; one `write_all` per complete line (concurrent hook processes share a file). A failed log write is swallowed — `hook` still exits 0. `open_role_file` and `write_detail` (`src/obs.rs`) run `strict::check_diagnostics` on the existing `diagnostics/` folder and on the role or detail file before `ensure_private_dir` narrows anything (a symlink refused, a folder held to the read rule, a file to the read rule on Unix and the write rule on Windows, an absent path passing): a refusal is a failed open — the role writer ends at `std::io::sink` and the detail line is dropped.

- Init order: panic hook first → clap → home/instance/role → home strict-modes (create first if new) → diagnostics dir/file checks and open → `config.json` → subscriber → `process-start`. Every `viola hook` arm but the two `--capture` arms (the event and dialog paths and `viola hook statusline`) runs its instance check (`canonical`, then `trusted`: `check_instance`) BEFORE this init (the role-file open sets an existing home to 0700, so a check made after it passes a widened home) and a refused or absent instance (a `VIOLA_DIR` naming no existing instance directory included) writes no line and opens no role file (exit 0 at once; the event and dialog paths also read no stdin, send no frame and make no SessionEnd append); its stdout carries the user's status-line output, never telemetry. Both `viola revive` arms (the start arm and `--list`) run their instance check before the log init as well: a refused check is the stderr pair, or under `--json` the `{"v":1,"error":"strict-modes-failed","detail":null}` document, and exit 1 with no log opened. `viola link` / `viola unlink` (on `instances/<driven>`) and `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause` and `release` (on their named instance; `send` after its text read) run `check_instance` on the home and the instance through the one `client::refuse_untrusted` before the log init too: a refusal is exit 21, the fixed instance-state pair or under `--json` the `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"strict-modes-failed"}` document, with no role file opened and the directory's mode left as found. `viola run` and `viola revive`'s start arm (after its instance check) run the home-tree check `strict::check_home_tree` (through `checked_exe`: the home, the `check_instance` set, `ledger/`, `bin/`, `plugin/`, `bin/<key>/`, the pinned copy, `plugin/<key>/` and its `hooks/` and `.claude-plugin/`, each that exists) before the wrapper log: a refusal is exit 1 with the home pair (the instance pair for an instance-level refusal; under `viola revive --json` the `strict-modes-failed` document), no log opened, no line and no child.

- Every line goes through `obs_event!` (defined in `viola_core::obs`): it attaches `event`, `process`, `instance` (from `ProcessCtx`); the caller passes `corr` as a typed field on the events that carry one; `message` is a static literal equal to the event name. Raw `tracing::{event,info,warn,error,debug,trace}!` is banned in two halves. Clippy `disallowed-macros` (`clippy.toml`) bans the level macros by path. Raw `event!` is caught by the fail-closed grep in `scripts/lint-probes.sh`, because on clippy 1.98.1 no allow inside `obs_event!` can exempt its inner `::tracing::event!` (obs-plan §3 logger-stack-install, D-33).
- `event` is a closed kebab-case enum (`ObsEvent`): a new value needs an obs Decisions Log entry and a `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` update.

- `corr` per event (JSON-RPC `id` · `dialog_id` · send `cursor`), copied as a number or string — never `?corr` / `%corr`, never renamed. A null `corr` / `instance` is key absence, never a literal `null`.

- Channel lines carry `conn = "<process>-<pid>-<t0>-<n>"`; wrapper `send-*` lines carry `conn` + `rpc_id`; `from` is logged with `from_trust:"self-reported"`, both absent on a line whose call carried no `from` (a `dialog-answered` for an answer that carried none, as on the hold's expiry line). On Unix a peer the wrapper's `accept_loop` refuses by euid (`peer_admitted`) is dropped on the accept thread, before its worker thread and before any frame, and writes no line by rule (no frame to key a line on); the client reads end-of-file.

- Log only fields named in obs-plan §6 (default-deny, enforced by G4). `detail` codes are closed kebab-case lists — never a path or pid. `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` closes `process-exit`'s at 20 values; exit 21's closed causes are `instance-dead`, `unwrapped-name`, `endpoint-lost`, `strict-modes-failed`, `server-verify-failed`, `socket-dir-refused` (`during` `call` for `endpoint-lost` alone; `instance-dead`, `unwrapped-name`, `server-verify-failed` and `socket-dir-refused` are `during` `connect`), and `stale-heartbeat` is exit 1's cause alone (a frame verb against a stale instance reads `instance-dead`). `channel-response` carries `detail` on a `-32602` only (`unsupported-version` · `invalid-params` · `release-from-driver`, from `ProtocolError::cause`, on the server's and the client's line alike, closed by `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`) and none on any other `channel-response` line, a refusal's included, whose own `detail` stays on `send-refused`.

- `#[instrument(skip_all, name = "<area>.<operation>", fields(..))]` or `info_span!` with an explicit field allow-list only — never bare `#[instrument]` (gate G1), never `err` / `ret` on anything that can carry a serde source or user content. Span names are static; no instance names, ids or paths.
- Spans are not serialized: pass `corr`, `conn`, `instance` as explicit values into threads/tasks.

- `panic = "unwind"` in every profile (gate G3). The panic hook writes one line to the role file (no stderr, never the default hook); `catch_unwind` at the main-thread catch site, around `hook` dispatch, the `run` pump and handle-wait threads, and the vt100 feed.

- `hook` → exit 0, empty stdout; `cli` → `process-exit{detail:"internal-error"}` when an instance resolves, then exit 1 with exactly `error: internal error` (no hint), or under `--json` (read from argv before any `--`) the `{"v":1,"error":"internal-error","detail":null}` document on stdout with stderr empty; `run` → `process-exit{detail:"internal-error"}` (the catch site prints nothing; under `viola revive --json` an anyhow error from `trusted`, `checked_exe`, `open_wrapper_log`, `preflight` or `start` prints the `internal-error` document before it returns, `pump_child`'s prints none); `mcp` main-thread → no `process-exit` line (`obs::internal_error_exit_line` covers `Run` and `Cli` only), then exit 1 with nothing on stdout. Exit 21's `--json` document carries one cause word of `viola_core::UnreachableCause` in `detail`, written by the one `unreachable_document` (`src/cmd/client.rs`; `refuse_untrusted` and `src/cmd/plugin.rs` through it), and the type writes no log line of its own.

- The detail-line `backtrace` is raw, never-symbolised frames (`src/panic_frames.rs`: `0x<ip> <module path> base=0x<base> +0x<offset>`, up to 62) — symbolising cost 351 of a 403 ms hook run on the Windows runner; never call `Backtrace::force_capture().to_string()` in a panic path.

- The hidden capture arms, `hook <event> --capture` and `hook statusline --capture` (the latter runs no instance check, no shell-out and no `budget.json` write, opens no role file and prints nothing), do no obs init and write no line (a bounded panic-line exemption, obs-plan §10). `viola verify` runs `strict::check_home_tree` on the home, `ledger/`, `bin/` and `plugin/` before its `cli` log opens: a refused tree is exit 1 with the home pair, no step line, no log and no line; a refused `update_stamps` (`StampsError::StrictModes`, nothing read or written) prints the same pair and exits 1 through its own `process-exit`, which under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME` carries `detail:"strict-modes-failed"`; every other refusal past the tree check writes its own code there (`batch-script-child`, `program-not-found`, `pinned-hash-mismatch`, `version-unreadable`, `unclean-fixture`), a failing row is no refusal and carries no code, and the fixture's `<file>` enters no code. A `viola verify` stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM (Unix `SIGINT` / `SIGTERM`, Windows Ctrl-C / Ctrl-Break) starts no further spawn, kills and reaps the child it is running, closes every spawn pair it opened (a child of an interactive PTY run killed at the stop closes with `duration_ms` and a `child_exit_status`, the PTY pump's exit code; a print-mode or `--version` probe child killed at the stop is not measured) and ends `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"interrupted"}` (a member of the `process-exit` `detail` enum `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` closes at 20 values); `run`'s version gate observes no stop.

- `viola list` (span `cli.list`) runs its strict-modes scan before its log; a refused scan (exit 21) opens no log and writes no line (obs-plan §10 exemption 7; the founder's own answer, 2026-10-13, superseding the operator's). Under a `VIOLA_NAME` it writes the self pair, one `parse-rejected{parser:"state-entry"}` per nonzero scan count, one `state-recovered` per replayed snapshot (its `instance` the caller, its `scanned` the scanned instance dir's own last component when it parses as a `ViolaName`, absent otherwise — never a path or a literal `null`), the `config-json` threshold rejections and one `agents-probe` spawn pair around its `claude agents --json` read (plus one `parse-rejected{parser:"claude-agents-json"}` on an oversize or malformed answer) into `cli-<name>.ndjson`; with no name it opens no log. `viola mcp`'s `list` tool makes the same board read (through `list::board_document`) and writes its `agents-probe` pair, `state-recovered`, `parse-rejected{parser:"state-entry"}` and `config-json` threshold lines into `mcp.ndjson`. `viola plugin install` runs its strict-modes tree check before its log; once it passes, under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME` it writes the self pair (`process-exit` exit 0, no detail) into `cli-<name>.ndjson`, and its span `cli.plugin_install` is no dispatch span: it is on `write_tree`, opened after the `cli` log opens, so the tree check and its refusal run outside it; no path in any line. `viola link` / `viola unlink` log as `cli` into the driven instance's `cli-<driven>.ndjson` (never the caller's `VIOLA_NAME`), their request inside spans `cli.link` / `cli.unlink`, once their instance check of it has passed.

- `viola revive`'s start arm logs as process `run` once its instance check has passed (`run-<name>.ndjson`, each preflight refusal — `already-live` (a live holder or a fresh replayed beat), `stale-heartbeat` (a stale holder), `no-session`, `session-live`, `cwd-missing` — one `process-exit{exit_code:1, detail}`; its `session-live` reading, skipped under `--fork` and passing on a failed read, writes one `process-start` / `process-exit{subject:"agents-probe"}` pair there, plus one `parse-rejected{parser:"claude-agents-json"}` on an oversize or malformed answer); `viola revive --list` is role `cli` (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract; the sixth exemption retired): after its strict-modes check passes and only under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME` it writes `process-start` / `process-exit` (`exit_code` 0 with no detail; `exit_code` 1 `detail:"no-session"` on an empty chain) into the caller's `cli-<VIOLA_NAME>.ndjson`, with no name no log, and its dispatch `Err` or panic reaches the `cli` catch site. A refused instance check on either `viola revive` arm (start or `--list`) or on `viola hook statusline`, or `viola mcp`'s refused `viola_state::strict::check_path` of its home or `diagnostics/` (run before its `mcp` role file opens; exit 1 with nothing on stdout or stderr), or `viola plugin install`'s refused `check_path` of its home or a `marketplace/` tree dir (run before its `cli` role file opens; exit 21, the stderr pair or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document), or `viola link` / `viola unlink`'s refused `check_instance` of the driven instance (run before their `cli` role file opens; exit 21, the fixed instance-state pair or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document), opens no role file and writes no line (the seventh exemption; on `viola hook statusline` the founder's own answer, 2026-10-13). So does a refused strict-modes check on the hook event and dialog paths (exit 0, nothing printed), on `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause` or `release` (exit 21, the instance pair or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document), on `viola verify`'s home tree (exit 1, the home pair) or on the home tree of `viola run` or `viola revive`'s start arm (exit 1, the home or the instance pair) (the eighth exemption). A refused peer euid (Unix) or a failed server check (the peer pid and start-time comparison on Linux and Windows; `server-verify-failed` reaches Linux, Windows and macOS, on macOS an euid mismatch alone, macOS comparing no peer pid, its named carve-out) sends no frame and opens no `channel.request`: the eight CLI frame verbs (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link`, `unlink`; `link` / `unlink` into the driven instance's `cli-<driven>.ndjson`) end `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:21, detail:"server-verify-failed", during:"connect"}` at WARN inside their dispatch span with no `channel-request` line; `viola hook` writes `hook-decision{detail:"server-verify-failed"}` at WARN (on a dialog hook `hook-invoked{corr:null}` first, then `decision_emitted:false`); MCP's frame tools return `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `server-verify-failed` and no line, as their refused `check_endpoint_dir` (made after `live_endpoint`) does with `detail` `socket-dir-refused` and no frame, and as the liveness pre-check's does with `without_endpoint`'s reading (`instance-dead` or `unwrapped-name`) and as their own refused `check_instance` of the home and the instance directory does (made before `live_endpoint`, `detail` `strict-modes-failed`, no frame); no pid, start time, path or endpoint in any line. A refused socket directory (`check_socket_dir`, the strict-modes read verdict) is none of these exemptions and writes under its own closed word `socket-dir-refused`, with no path, pid or uid in any line: `viola run` and `viola revive`'s start (`socket_dir_ready`, no span, before any snapshot, child or `Server::bind`; a failed create, a lost race and a refused check read one code, and a `Server::bind` failure is not this refusal) one `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"socket-dir-refused"}`, under `viola revive --json` the same-shaped `socket-dir-refused` document; the eight CLI frame verbs one `process-exit{exit_code:21, detail:"socket-dir-refused", during:"connect"}` at WARN inside their dispatch span, no `channel-request` line and no frame; `viola hook` one `hook-decision{detail:"socket-dir-refused"}` at WARN inside `hook.handle` (on a dialog hook after `hook-invoked{corr:null}`, with `decision_emitted:false`), exit 0, empty streams and no frame.

- `run.budget_eval` (INTERNAL; `trigger` `start|send|turn-ended`, `paused`, `window` only when paused) is declared once and opened once per evaluation; at start it sits between `channel.bind` and `state.snapshot_write`. `read_budget` and `release --budget`'s lift carry no span and no line of their own; `budget-gate` is appended only when (paused, window, override end) changes. The implicit link record on a `send` or an `answer`, the explicit `link` / `unlink` methods the driven wrapper serves (their trace the call's `channel-request` / `channel-response` pair, which holds neither name), the link set's restore at start and the replay's link rule carry no span and no process-log line of their own; `driver`, `driven` and `since` reach no home-level line. A `budget-paused` refusal's `send-refused` line carries `window`, `used_percentage`, `resets_at` and `paused:true`. At a dialog hold's end (`run.dialog_await`'s `deadline_ms`, `config.json`'s `dialog_hold_s` in ms, 60 000–3 600 000, default 60 000) the wrapper appends one `dialog-expired{dialog_id, dialog_kind}` product line and writes one `dialog-answered{corr:<dialog_id>, dialog_kind, deadline_hit:true, duration_ms}` with no `from` / `from_trust`; a hand-back or an answer writes neither; the hook then writes `hook-decision{decision_emitted:false, deadline_hit:false}`, `deadline_hit:true` only when its own read times out at its backstop bound `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX + 5 s` (3605 s).
- No per-byte or per-line logging in hot loops (PTY pump); no line per heartbeat tick — transitions only.

- 2026-09-24: `obs_event!` expands to `::tracing::event!`, so a raw-log census greps `tracing::(info|warn|error|debug|trace)!` — a bare `tracing::` grep reads the sanctioned macro in `viola_core::obs` as a raw call.

Universal security requirements for viola. Apply to all files. This rule file has no `paths:` frontmatter — it loads unconditionally, so it stays lean; the full contract is `.andromeda/security-plan.md` (tier Minimal with local-boundary elevations).
- Secrets in v1: inherited `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN` / `_SOCKET` and every R8-stripped `CLAUDE*` value. None may reach a log, diagnostic, event, snapshot, fixture or error body.
- Never commit `.env*`, local `--home` test directories, tokens, cookies or signing material; never hardcode a credential in source or in the `include_str!` plugin files.

- Windows pipe listener: explicit protected SDDL `D:P(A;;GA;;;<user-SID>)(A;;GA;;;SY)`, `accept_remote(false)`, first-instance, non-inheritable. Client opens with `SECURITY_SQOS_PRESENT | SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION` — never interprocess's default connect.

- Unix socket: a verified 0700 per-user dir (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/viola/`, `$TMPDIR/viola/`, `/tmp/viola-<uid>/`), never `/tmp` root, never abstract namespace, the socket chmod 0600 after the bind as a secondary control only (never `ListenerOptionsExt::mode`: `Unsupported` on macOS fails the bind), `peer_creds` euid on both sides (the wrapper drops a refused peer in `accept_loop` before any frame; a client refuses a peer whose euid cannot be read), `try_overwrite` off. The directory check (`check_socket_dir`, and `check_endpoint_dir` on a recorded endpoint's parent: owner == `geteuid()`, `mode & 0o077 == 0`, not a symlink, never a chmod) runs before the bind and before any client connect, at the seams and never inside `viola_channel::Client::connect`; `run` and the start of `revive` refuse before any snapshot, child or `Server::bind`, a failed create and a refused check alike: exit 1, `socket-dir-refused`, one `process-exit`.

- Before the FIRST frame of any method (including `hook.event`), verify the server: pid (+ sysinfo start time) against a `snapshot.json` that passed strict-modes in the same process (the peer euid checked too on Unix, never skipped; macOS, where the peer reports no pid, compares no pid or start time, the named carve-out, owned by no route entry). `viola hook`'s event and dialog paths run `check_instance` on the canonicalised instance (`canonical`, then `trusted`, in `src/cmd/hook.rs`) before the diagnostics level and obs init; a refused or absent instance exits 0 at once with no `config.json` read, no stdin read, no line and no frame; the two `--capture` arms stay ahead of the check. `verify` checks its home tree (`check_home_tree`: the home, `ledger/`, `bin/`, `plugin/`) before its `cli` log, and its `update_stamps` runs `strict::check_stamps` before it creates `ledger/` and again under its lock (a refusal `StampsError::StrictModes` reads and writes nothing, exit 1 with the home pair); `run`'s version gate reads the stamps through `read_stamps_strict` (a refusal is `cli_verified:false`). On Windows x64 `run`'s `pin_companions` runs `check_present` on `bin/<version>-<hash>/conpty/` and on each companion that exists before the held open and the SHA-256 re-hash (a refusal writes and loads nothing, the child runs on the inbox ConPTY, `sideload_fallback` `strict-modes-failed`). No dated strict-modes gap remains: every other frame client runs `check_instance` first, then reads the snapshot through `read_snapshot_or_replay` (a replayed or absent one gives no endpoint and so no frame), then the liveness-only pre-check, the socket-directory check on the recorded endpoint (`check_endpoint_dir`), the connect, on Unix the peer euid decision (`peer_admitted`) and, on Linux and Windows, the server check — CLI `send` (after its text read), `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link` and `unlink` through `client::refuse_untrusted`, then `live_endpoint` (the snapshot's pid + start time alive, the heartbeat live, an `endpoint` present; else exit 21, `viola_state::liveness::without_endpoint`'s `symlink_metadata`, which opens nothing and writes no line, reading `instance-dead` for an instance directory and `unwrapped-name` for anything else), then `client::connect` (the socket-directory check on the recorded endpoint, the connect, on Unix the peer euid decision and, on Linux and Windows, the peer pid and its start time against the snapshot's `pid` and `started_at`); `viola hook pre-tool-use|permission-request` past `trusted` writes its `hook.dialog` frame after its payload shape check through `src/cmd/hook.rs`'s shared `connect`; `viola mcp`'s `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` tools through the Tokio client after `check_instance` and `viola_state::liveness::live_endpoint` (else `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `without_endpoint`'s reading, `instance-dead` or `unwrapped-name`) then `check_endpoint_dir` (a refusal `socket-dir-refused`) and, after `TokioClient::connect`, the peer euid decision (a refusal `server-verify-failed`) and the server check. On a strict-modes refusal no frame and no line is written: the CLI frame verbs exit 21 with the instance `unable:` / `hint:` pair (under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document, `detail` `strict-modes-failed`), `hook` exits 0 with no body, MCP returns `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `strict-modes-failed`. On a refused socket directory, before the connect, no frame is written: the CLI frame verbs exit 21 `instance-unreachable` (under `--json`, `detail` `socket-dir-refused`), MCP returns `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `socket-dir-refused` and writes no line, and `hook` fails open (exit 0, no body, one WARN `hook-decision` carrying `socket-dir-refused`). On a mismatch, a refused peer euid, or a check that cannot be made, no frame is written: the CLI frame verbs exit 21 `instance-unreachable` (under `--json`, `detail` `server-verify-failed`), MCP returns `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `server-verify-failed` and writes no line, and `hook` fails open (exit 0, no body, `hook-decision` carrying `server-verify-failed`); no line or output holds a pid, start time, path or endpoint.

- The hidden `hook <event> --capture <DIR>` (founder-ratified, Decisions Log `2026-09-28`) is `viola verify`'s probe capture only: absolute existing `<DIR>`, stdin through `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)`, raw 0600 write, no `VIOLA_*` read, no obs init, no channel, exit 0 always; its statusline form `hook statusline --capture <DIR> [--shell <WORD>]` (Run B's probe settings only; the founder's own answer to P4 fork 3 of chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows) holds the same bounds, writes the payload raw and only the closed `ShellVerdict` (`bin-sh` · `other`, never the word), and prints nothing. No other caller may register it.

- Home: 0700 dirs, 0600 files via `OpenOptionsExt::mode` (pinned `bin/<version>-<hash>/viola` is 0700); every replaced file goes through the one helper `viola_state::fs::replace_private` (tempfile `persist`), which sets the temp file's mode before any byte is written; the pinned `viola` is never replaced: its absent copy goes through `viola_state::fs::place_private_new` (mode 0700 set before any byte, `sync_all`, the write handle closed, then `persist_noclobber`, never over a present name), and a copy another start placed first is re-hashed before reuse, different bytes left as found. Strict-modes check (Unix mode/owner; Windows owner + DACL incl. inherit-only and generic bits, NULL DACL, non-persistent-ACL volume) at every entry point that reads `snapshot.json`, `ledger/stamps.json` or `statusline_command`, before its first read or open under the home (`run`, `revive`'s start and `verify` through `check_home_tree` before their log opens, exit 1; `viola list`'s `board::scan` through `check_read` on the home on every OS (a home another user may read refused with or without an instance; that rule stands on a delegate's answer, OPEN, owner the Epoch 7 boundary batch), `check_path` on `instances/` and `check_instance` per instance, the whole board refused, exit 21; the frame verbs through `check_instance`, exit 21; the diagnostics opens through `check_diagnostics`, a refusal a failed open), refusing also a home, instance directory or `diagnostics/` another user can read (Unix any group or other bit; Windows a read grant to another SID, inherit-only included) and a symlinked `diagnostics/` folder or file, and in `viola plugin install` on its home and each existing `marketplace/` tree dir before anything is created or opened (exit 21); `marketplace/` is no trusted file and its installed `command` is not re-hashed (`marketplace/` is off the integrity set).

- Every exec-form `command` in `hooks.json`, `.mcp.json` and the `settings.json` statusline is the absolute pinned path, and in `viola plugin install`'s `marketplace/viola/.mcp.json` the canonical exe that ran the install (`args` `["--home", <the canonical home>, "mcp"]`) — never a PATH lookup. Rewrite `plugin/` atomically on every start, and on Unix the instance's `settings.json` statusline override (`replace_private`, 0600, only for a pinned path of ASCII letters, digits and `_ - . / :`; none on Windows; passed as `--settings <instance dir>/settings.json` after `--plugin-dir`, a founder-ratified widening, live, 2026-10-10); re-hash (truncated SHA-256) a pinned exe before reuse; never FNV/`DefaultHasher` for it.

Path-scoped rules for the agent-driven harness driver: the `scripts/agent-run.*` shims, `viola-harness`, the rstest fixture chains and the fake agent.
**Authoritative sources (bound):**
- `.andromeda/test-plan.md` §3 — the 5-command contract, status shape, log format, session record, test data bootstrap
- `.andromeda/obs-plan.md` §3 — the log sinks, the `event` enum, `corr` / `conn`, null-as-absence

viola is a standalone, cross-platform (Windows first) bridge that lets one interactive Claude Code session drive another on the user's own subscription. It wraps the unmodified `claude` CLI in a pseudo-terminal, types at turn boundaries, answers dialogs through hooks, and holds a one-driver wheel the human can take at any moment; a minimal view-only frontend is deferred to 0.2.0 (its technology is not chosen).

<!-- GENERATED:setup:architecture start -->
viola is mechanism, not policy: it carries typed input, answers dialogs when told to, logs everything and holds the wheel, but never decides what to answer — driver-side policy (Andromeda's decision rights included) stays outside the binary. Every behaviour of the `claude` CLI it relies on is a measured, version-stamped capability-ledger row; on an unverified CLI build viola degrades to transport-only and every send is confirmed after the fact (`prompt-submitted` read-back or a ledger post-condition), never presumed, the one exception a ledger-listed local command whose post-condition is none or not yet measured on this CLI version: `ok` with `confirmed: false`, detail `unconfirmable`.

There is no daemon: each wrapper (a `viola run`, or a `viola revive` whose preflight passed) owns one local-socket endpoint (named pipe / per-user Unix socket), every other verb is a separate process, and the shared truth is the disk — ndjson append logs and atomic snapshots that survive a crash on either side. It is a modular monolith: one binary around compiler-enforced crates (`pty · channel · state · agent-claude · mcp` around `core`), built and CI-tested on Windows, macOS and Linux from the first commit, with Windows the first target (the first live run was on the Linux dev host).

_This section is curated by `/wrap-session`. It accumulates universal (Tier 1) rules captured from work sessions — rules that apply to every file and every task. Do not edit manually during wrap-session runs — changes are preserved but wrap-session appends new entries here._
- Prompt text reaches viola only from stdin or `--file`, never from a leading-slash argument (Git Bash rewrites `/skill` into a Windows path).
- `viola release` is a human verb: no driver-facing hint, MCP tool or doc suggests it to a driver (a `release` carrying `from` is refused `-32602`).
- Design against the installed `claude` CLI, measured: the docs lag the build, so an unmeasured behaviour is a ledger row to probe, not an assumption.

- Every viola format carries `v` except process-log lines, whose version is their schema filename (`diag-line.v1.json`); readers skip and count unknown kinds and fields, and never use `deny_unknown_fields` on viola's own formats (mixed binary versions are real). [corrected 2026-09-24: the diag-line default-deny field list admits no `v`]

- Probe, baseline and gate a CI tool at the exact version CI pins — install that version on the host first; an older host tool accepts flags the pinned one rejects, so a plan written against it ships gate commands that cannot pass.
- A claim that reaches a wrap only through a relayed direction, with no artifact on disk behind it, is carried as a labelled HYPOTHESIS on the route, never written into a spec master as fact.
- A red stays open until its cause is known: a green re-run never closes it, and a red met during a chunk folds into that chunk even outside its diff.
- A tool call refused with no verdict by the permission classifier is a transient outage, not a gate to route around: fill the wait with read-only work and retry the same call.

- A master, a key file or a leaf names a working-route entry by its title, never by a bare route line number: the number goes stale at every insertion ahead of the entry, and the citation sweep reads no bare number.

- A count written into a master carries the rule that produced it (the pattern or the named list) beside the number, and a count found without one is read back to the sidecar entry that wrote it before it is amended. Extended 2026-10-16: a master states no test-case count at all — it names the functions, and the code's `#[case]` rows are the count. Extended 2026-10-26: a count a plan or research states is taken by its master's rule too, never by a wider listing.
- A missing test for a clause a chunk landed is folded into the next chunk, never pinned on a later route entry.

- A planned step or master amendment that departs from a founder ruling is never a decisive lean or a card-confirm item: plan up to it, hold it behind a stop rule naming what counts as his word, and raise it at P4 as a fork; his answer covers only what the question shown to him named, never the wider item its number points to.

- A capability whose built surface falls short of its claimed acceptance is un-claimed with a dated note naming the gap and the route entry that owns it, never refined down to what was built so that it reads verified.

- A timestamp written into any record (a report's date, an evidence or journal stamp) is read from `date -u` at the moment it is written, never estimated or carried forward: the stamp-ahead hook refuses an estimate, and a script that fires no hook lands it unchecked.
